summary: Replace the rejected parameter-action proposal with exact mu-sensitivity, zero-action, regular-chart norm-criticality, and spectral-frontier tangent identities while preserving the all-n O3a target as open.

node.title: Parameter action and spectral-frontier identities for the relay curve
node.statement: The accepted full-relay and symplectic nested-relay claims, exact parameter-dependent saltation, Hamiltonian parameter variation, zero signed action, and unit-interval scaling imply the mu-sensitivity pairing, action one-form, regular-chart norm-criticality, and spectral-frontier tangent identities in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-PARAMETER-ACTION-R1.

node.title: Exact mu-sensitivity, zero-action, and regular-chart unit-slope reduction
node.statement: Fix finite R>1, n>=2, either relay sign, and a premise-complete transverse common-terminal trajectory with mu>1 and q>1. Let nu=partial_mu(U,U_t,V,V_t) at fixed q and fixed physical time, including the parameter-dependent saltation term, and retain p=U_t(L), r=V_t(L). Then -p nu_U(L)+r nu_V(L)=2mu I_V(L) and partial_mu A_n=(1-q^2)nu_U(L)/(p r^2)+2mu I_V(L)/r^2. No sign for partial_mu A_n follows at a q-Jacobi conjugate point because nu_U is an independent mu-sensitivity. Along every differentiable common-terminal sheet the zero signed action gives ((1-q^2)/2)dL=mu I_V dmu. On a regular mu chart, B=I_U-I_V equals ((1-q^2)sqrt(mu^2-1)/(2mu)) d_mu[L sqrt(mu^2-1)], so equal norm is exactly criticality of sqrt(lambda_(n+1)-lambda_n)=L sqrt(mu^2-1) on that chart. Equivalently, for a=L^2, b=mu^2L^2 and c=I_U/I_V, the relay spectral curve obeys the tangent one-form db=c da; when da is nonzero its slope is c, and complete roots have unit slope. The dmu=0 and da=0 cases are kept as degenerate one-form statements. These identities do not prove graphness, curvature, exclude disconnected reflected sheets, or settle universal O3a.

node.title: Prove common-terminal graph order and one unit-slope spectral point
node.statement: Upgrade the exact parameter-action reduction to a global all-chamber theorem: make the common-terminal set a single reflection-fixed graph with no q-Jacobi conjugate point and prove that c=I_U/I_V=db/da crosses one exactly once; alternatively certify a distinct complete reflected pair or two unit-slope spectral points.
node.formal_statement: For every finite R>1, n>=2 and max/min sign, prove fixed-mu uniqueness of A_n(mu,q)=0 over all premise-complete chambers and compatible closures, then prove strict one-crossing of c=I_U/I_V through 1 on the resulting spectral curve; or provide interval-certified distinct complete roots satisfying all phase, relay, event-count, norm, and indexing predicates.
discharge_criteria: Cover every finite R>1, every n>=2, both saturation signs, every premise-complete relay chamber, and compatible chamber closures.
A local derivative sign, a finite numerical scan, or curvature at only symmetric points is insufficient.
A spectral-curve argument must separately exclude a nonfixed reflection fiber because reflection preserves both eigenvalues and c.
A counterexample must be interval-certified with exact mode indices, 2n transverse events, correct sign law, positive cells, common terminal time, and equal integrals.

node.title: Parameter-action and spectral-frontier continuation route
node.statement: Use exact mu sensitivity and zero action to turn norm equality into a unit-slope condition on the common-terminal spectral curve, while testing the two remaining requirements: fixed-mu graph order and single crossing of c=I_U/I_V through one.
node.method_family: Parameter-dependent symplectic saltation, zero Hamilton action, spectral-frontier tangent geometry, fixed-mu root order, bounded reflected-pair search, and interval escalation
node.deliverable_contract: A global graph plus one-unit-slope theorem, a certified distinct reflected pair, or an audited precise obstruction preserving the universal target as open.
falsification_tests: Retain the explicit h_mu saltation term and verify its event pairing cancellation rather than treating mu as an ordinary smooth parameter.
Do not infer a fold from partial_q A_n=0 without a nonzero second derivative.
Do not infer global curvature from db=(I_U/I_V)da or from finitely many derivative signs.
Reject sign-change brackets that land on relay chamber discontinuities or have the wrong 2n event count.
Treat high-n/high-R optimizer failure as no conclusion.
node.expected_bottleneck: A fixed-sign hybrid twist or embedded spectral-frontier theorem strong enough to exclude both conjugate points and disconnected reflection pairs.

rationale.scope: The exact identities give a parameter-sensitivity pairing and reduce equal norm to a scalar unit-slope/criticality condition only on the stated regular charts. They imply no mu-transversality at a q-Jacobi point and do not prove global graphness, spectral curvature, symmetry, or uniqueness.
rationale.computation_policy: The 120 fixed-mu branch scans, 32 retained roots, derivative probes, event probes, and high-n/high-R multistarts are finite binary64 discovery evidence only. Seven discontinuous or wrong-chamber sign brackets were rejected and no candidate survived for interval certification.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Finite R>1, n>=2, both signs, premise-complete common-terminal relay trajectories and their indexed zero times and relay integrals.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The action and spectral scaling are applied only on the accepted common-terminal relay class; equal norm is withheld until the derived criticality equivalence.

math_premise_contracts.scope: The exact q-Jacobi derivative, common-terminal energy, reflection map, and fixed-point diagnostic on transverse q>1 chambers.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The new inference reuses the established q-Jacobi formula and adds an independently derived mu sensitivity and action identity. The two sensitivities are not identified, so no mu-transversality or still-open no-conjugate theorem is imported.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Positive box-constrained weighted Dirichlet strings, unit-interval scaling, and the adjacent indexed gap.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The variables a=L^2 and b=mu^2L^2 are exactly the two unit-interval indexed eigenvalues, so L sqrt(mu^2-1) is the square root of the canonical adjacent gap.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Both max/min relay laws, 2n effective switches, and a.e. switch representatives.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The parameter-dependent event algebra treats both signs and never uses point values of rho at switches.

ordered_steps: Write the exact fixed-time mu-sensitivity jump as nu_+=Xi nu_-+a h_mu/(nabla h dot f_-), retaining h_mu=-2mu V^2.
Use Xi xi=xi, symplecticity, and omega(xi,a)=-Delta rho h=0 to prove that the extra surface-parameter term does not jump omega(xi,nu).
Inside every material cell identify the inhomogeneous forcing g_mu=(0,0,0,-2mu rho V) and integrate d_t omega(xi,nu)=2mu rho V^2 to obtain -p nu_U+r nu_V=2mu I_V.
Differentiate the two simple terminal zero times and combine the preceding pairing with p^2-r^2=1-q^2 to obtain the exact partial_mu A_n formula.
Keep nu_U as an independent mu-sensitivity: the established q-conjugate condition constrains eta=partial_q z only, so it does not simplify or sign the partial_mu A_n formula.
Use the signed Lagrangian, common Dirichlet endpoints, integration by parts, and 2Phi=rho S to prove that the action vanishes on every common-terminal sheet.
Differentiate the zero action with moving endpoint and explicit mu parameter to get ((1-q^2)/2)dL=mu I_V dmu, including the sign of the -H dL endpoint term.
On a regular mu chart, combine this one-form with I_U-mu^2I_V=L(1-q^2)/2 to express B=I_U-I_V as a nonzero factor times d_mu[L sqrt(mu^2-1)].
Rescale to the unit interval to identify L^2 and mu^2L^2 as lambda_n and lambda_(n+1), proving the adjacent-gap criticality formula only on the regular mu chart.

Normalize the two modes and differentiate b-c a with c=I_U/I_V along the relay interface motion; the switching density is proportional to S and vanishes at every interface, yielding the tangent one-form db=c da.
Separate the resulting unit-slope spectral condition from the still-open curvature, graphness, and reflection-fiber obligations.
boundary_cases: Every finite R>1, n>=2, and both relay signs are covered only on premise-complete transverse common-terminal sheets with mu,q>1 and simple terminal zeros.
R=1, R=infinity, grazing events, and unresolved chamber boundaries are not included.
At dmu=0 the action relation is kept as a one-form and is not divided by dmu; the norm-criticality equivalence is not asserted there.
A stationary projection is not called a fold without second-order information.
At da=0 the tangent relation is not divided by da; unit tangent slope is asserted only when da is nonzero and is not promoted to unique curvature.
A spectral point is not promoted to a unique coefficient because reflection is isospectral.
No finite numerical derivative or root scan is used in the proof.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: The corrected exact identities expose graph order, curvature, and reflection-fiber injectivity as separate missing theorems. None is discharged by the finite scans, and no local mu transversality has been proved.
The route adds a proved exact reduction and stronger falsification filters but neither proves the universal max/min claims nor produces a certifiable distinct root pair.
